core_obligations: Recover the underlying map on opens (proof lines 5307-5317): from the 2-isomorphism t on inverse image functors, and the fact that both a_{small}^{-1}h_V = h_{a^{-1}(V)} and b_{small}^{-1}h_V = h_{b^{-1}(V)} are subsheaves of the final sheaf, conclude that t must be the identity there and hence a^{-1}(V) = b^{-1}(V) for every open V, so a and b agree on underlying topological spaces.

Use sections of the structure sheaf (proof lines 5318-5336): a section f in O_Y(V) is the same as a map h_V -> O_Y; pulling back and applying t produces the displayed commutative diagram, whose triangle is commutative by definition of a 2-isomorphism in the 2-category of ringed topoi.

Conclude equality of morphisms (proof lines 5337-5343): since the top horizontal composite comes from the identity a^{-1}(V) = b^{-1}(V), commutativity of the diagram forces a_{small}^sharp(f) = b_{small}^sharp(f) in O_X(a^{-1}(V)) = O_X(b^{-1}(V)); as this holds for all V and f, the morphisms of schemes a and b are equal.
proof_roadmap: Use that the sheaves h_V are subsheaves of the final sheaf to show the 2-isomorphism is the identity on them.
Deduce that a and b induce the same map on open subsets of Y.
For a section of the structure sheaf, read the 2-isomorphism as the displayed commutative diagram.
Commutativity forces equal structural maps, so the two morphisms of schemes agree.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the small morphism of ringed topoi remembers the morphism of schemes: two morphisms a, b : X -> Y with 2-isomorphic small ringed topoi are equal (statement lines 5297-5304). The proof separates two layers. First, because the sheaves h_V are subsheaves of the final sheaf, the 2-isomorphism has to be the identity on each of them, which recovers a^{-1}(V) = b^{-1}(V) and hence equality on underlying topological spaces (proof lines 5309-5317). Second, a section f of O_Y(V) is a map h_V -> O_Y, and pulling back along the 2-isomorphism yields the displayed diagram whose commutativity, by definition of a 2-isomorphism of ringed topoi, forces the two structural maps to agree (proof lines 5318-5341). The non-formal content is the interplay of the two layers. The claim is H2: two short arguments, each ending in an equality of maps.
